title: Septoria Blotch on Winter Wheat in Eastern and Western Russian Regions: Species Composition of Pathogens and Characterization of Parastagonospora spp. Populations Based on NE-Effector Genes
content: Septoria blotch is one of the most harmful diseases of bread wheat and leads to significant losses of grain harvest worldwide. The main causative agents of the disease are hemibiotrophic species Zymoseptoria tritici, Parastagonospora nodorum and Parastagonospora pseudonodorum. Parastagonospora spp. produce a set of necrotrophic effectors (NE-effectors, SnToxs) during their interaction with wheat plants. Information on the distribution of the pathogen species across regions, and on the characterization of Parastagonospora spp. with respect to the SnTox genes encoding NE-effectors, is important for the genetic protection of wheat. The research was conducted in three Russian regions (Tambov, Omsk, and Novosibirsk). The ratio of the pathogenic species on winter bread wheat, as well as the distribution of the SnToxA, SnTox1, SnTox3, SnTox267, and SnTox5 genes in populations of Parastagonospora spp., was studied using PCR analysis. The results showed that Z. tritici dominates on wheat crops in the Tambov region and is rarely found in the Siberian regions. The SnTox1 gene was absent from the populations of both Parastagonospora spp., although isolates with unidentified NE-genes accounted for a significant proportion of the Siberian populations. SnToxA was present at a high frequency only in the Tambov P. pseudonodorum population. SnTox5 was represented at the highest frequency in all populations. SnTox3 was present at a relatively high frequency in the Siberian P. nodorum populations, as well as in the Tambov and Novosibirsk P. pseudonodorum populations. The SnTox267 gene was detected at a high frequency only in the Omsk P. nodorum population. The significance of the NE-genes for pathogen development increases in the series ‘SnTox267 – SnToxA – SnTox3 – SnTox5’.
